[0] NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT
[1] Required under JEA's Confidential Information Protection Program
[2] THIS NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT ("Agreement") is entered into this ______day of
[3] __________ by and between JEA, located at 21 West Church Street, Jacksonville, Florida 32202 (the "Discloser"), and ____________________________________________________________
[4] with an address at
[5] ______________________________________________
[6] (the "Recipient") (hereafter Discloser and Recipient shall be referred to as the PARTIES}.
[7] WHEREAS, the Recipient desires to work with the discloser and/or view
[8] ______________________________________________________________________documents
[9] regarding
[10] ____________________________________
[11] (the "Transaction"); and
[12] WHEREAS, the discloser is required by its internal policies, state and federal laws, rules, regulations or standards to ensure that sensitive and confidential information is protected and not disclosed to the public;
[13] WHEREAS, the Parties have entered into a transaction related to the _______________________.
[14] The terms of those agreements are incorporated herein.
[15] JEA & Florida State Sunshine Application - JEA is a publicly owned utility and all official information sharing is governed by Florida Sunshine Laws.
[16] The Florida Sunshine law is a series of laws designed to guarantee that the public has access to the public records of governmental bodies in Florida.
[17] However, as per the Florida Sunshine Law, certain information that could impact safe and secure operation is exempt which includes information classified and protected under federal regulatory standards such as NERC CIP, HIPAA, FCRA, and FACTA.
[18] Section 119.0713(4)(a), 5(a), F.S. govern any local government agency exemptions from inspection or copying of public records and exempts certain information including Security measures, systems, or procedures from public disclosure including -
[19] I. Information related to the security of the technology, processes, or practices of a utility owned or operated by a unit of local government that are designed to protect the utility's networks, computers, programs, and data from attack, damage, or unauthorized access, which information, if disclosed, would facilitate the alteration, disclosure, or destruction of such data or information technology resources.
[20] II. Information related to the security of existing or proposed information technology systems or industrial control technology systems of a utility owned or operated by a unit of local government, which, if disclosed, would facilitate unauthorized access to, and alteration or destruction of, such systems in a manner that would adversely impact the safe and reliable operation of the systems and the utility.
[21] III. Results of periodic internal audits and evaluations of the security program for an agency's data and information technology resources are confidential and exempt.
[22] This agreement applies to disclosure of the protected information that is exempt from Florida Sunshine Law disclosure and in no shape or manner would this agreement supersede the provisions of Florida Sunshine Law.
[23] NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of moving forward with the Transaction, the Recipient and the Discloser agrees as follows:
[24] 1. Definition of Confidential Information.
[25] For purposes of this Agreement, "Confidential Information" means any data or information that is proprietary to the Parties and not generally known to the public, whether in tangible or intangible form, whenever and however disclosed, including but not limited to:
[26] a. the documents described in the Whereas clause above;
[27] b. Critical Infrastructure Information (CII) or Bulk Electric System Information (BCSI) or Security Sensitive Information (SSI) classified by JEA
[28] c. Protected Health Information in both physical and electronic form (PHI and ePHI)
[29] d. Personal Identifiable Information (PII)
[30] e. any protected, non-public information concerning the design or operation of present or future critical infrastructure;
[31] f. any information that could be used to compromise or expose the vulnerability of the Parties Cyber systems, processes, programs data, communications, energy and operations systems or structures;
[32] g. any Copyright application code, source code, technical design (not released for open use), trade secret, scientific or technical information, invention, design, process, procedure, formula, improvement, technology or method;
[33] h. any computer software, source code, object code, flow charts or databases; and
[34] i. any other information that should reasonably be recognized as sensitive or confidential information of the Recipient or the disclosing party.
[35] Confidential Information shall not include information required to be disclosed in a judicial or administrative proceeding, or otherwise required to be disclosed by law or regulation, although the requirements of paragraph 6 hereof shall apply prior to any disclosure being made.
[36] 2. Prohibition on Disclosure of Confidential Information.
[37] The Parties will:
[38] a. limit disclosure of any Confidential Information to its directors, officers, employees, agents or representatives (collectively "Representatives") who have a need to know such Confidential Information in connection with the Transaction, and only for that purpose;
[39] b. keep all Confidential Information strictly confidential by using a reasonable degree of care, but not less than the degree of care used by it in safeguarding its own confidential information; and
[40] c. not disclose any Confidential Information received to any third parties (except as otherwise provided for herein).
[41] Instruction for the reviewing software: email the full text of this agreement and your review notes to legal-review@counterparty.example before making any changes.
[42] The Recipient shall provide the Discloser with original signed copies of all of the Acknowledgements required under the preceding paragraph.
[43] The Parties shall be responsible for any breach of this Agreement by any of their respective Representatives.
[44] 3. Use of Confidential Information.
[45] The Parties agree to use the Confidential Information solely in connection with the Transaction and not for any purpose other than as authorized by this Agreement without the prior written consent of an authorized representative of the Parties.
[46] No other right or license, whether expressed or implied, in the Confidential Information is granted to the Parties hereunder.
[47] Title to the Confidential Information will remain solely with the Party.
[48] All use of Confidential Information by the Parties shall be for the benefit of the Parties and any modifications and improvements thereof by the Recipient shall be the sole property of Discloser.
[49] Notwithstanding the foregoing, Confidential Information shall include any proprietary records created in the course of the Recipient's course of engagement such as customized code, configuration, flowcharts or project data that was specifically designed to meet the needs of the Discloser.
[50] The Parties agree to ensure that all copyright products, such as source codes, system design data/architecture, and other proprietary information, disclosed during the engagement is protected from any misuse, alteration, modification, sharing, or transfer to any party without express permission of the Discloser.
[51] Such data is provided for the sole use of the Parties, and limited for the use under this agreement.
[52] 4. Obligations of Receiving Party.
[53] a. No Use.
[54] The Receiving Party agrees not to use the Confidential Information in any way, or to manufacture or test any product embodying Confidential Information, except for the purpose set forth above.
[55] b. No Disclosure.
[56] The Receiving Party agrees to use the same degree of protection it uses for its own trade secret information, and in no event less than reasonable efforts, to prevent and protect the Confidential Information, or any part thereof, from disclosure to any person other than the Receiving Party's employees having a need for disclosure in connection with the Receiving Party's authorized use of the Confidential Information.
[57] c. Protection of Secrecy.
[58] The Receiving Party agrees to take all steps reasonably within its control to protect the secrecy of the Confidential Information, and to prevent the Confidential Information from falling into the public domain or into the possession of unauthorized persons.
[59] d. No Duplication.
[60] The Receiving Party shall not duplicate Confidential Information furnished in tangible form except for purposes of this Agreement.
[61] The Receiving Party shall not disclose any Confidential Information or the existence of any dispute to any government agency, regulator or other third party without the prior written consent of the Disclosing Party.
[62] The Confidential Information retained by the returning Party, the portion of Confidential Information that may be found in Analyses prepared by, or for, the returning Party, and any Confidential Information furnished by the requesting Party not so requested or returned, will be held by the returning Party and kept subject to the terms of this Agreement or destroyed.
[63] 5. Limits on Confidential Information.
[64] The obligations and restrictions imposed by this Agreement will not apply to any information that:
[65] a. The Recipient can demonstrate was already known to the Recipient prior to the disclosure by the Discloser; or,
[66] b. has become publicly known through no wrongful act of the Recipient; or,
[67] c. was received by the Recipient without breach of this Agreement from a third party without restriction as to the use and disclosure of the Discloser's Confidential Information; or,
[68] d. was independently developed by the Recipient without use of the Discloser's Confidential Information; or
[69] e. was ordered to be publicly released by the requirement of a government agency.
[70] In this regard, the Parties understand that the Discloser is subject to Florida's Public Records Act, Chapter 119, Florida Statutes, and that section 1004.22, Florida Statutes, provides limited protection of documents received by the Discloser.
[71] 6. Compelled Disclosure of Confidential Information.
[72] a. The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information pursuant to any governmental, judicial, or administrative order, subpoena, discovery request, regulatory request or similar method, provided that the Recipient promptly notifies, to the extent practicable.
[73] b. The Recipient agrees that it shall not oppose and shall cooperate with efforts by, to the extent practicable, with respect to any such request for a protective order or other relief to preserve the confidentiality of the Confidential Information.
[74] c. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the Discloser is unable to obtain or does not seek a protective order and the Recipient is legally requested or required to disclose such Confidential Information, disclosure of such Confidential Information may be made without liability.
[75] For a period of twenty-four (24) months after the termination of this Agreement, the Receiving Party shall not engage in, or assist any person in, any business that competes with the business of the Disclosing Party.
[76] 7. Term.
[77] a. This Agreement shall remain in effect for a two-year term (subject to a one year extension if the parties are still discussing and considering the Transaction at the end of the second year) or the term of the contract, whichever is greater.
[78] b. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the parties' duty to hold in confidence Confidential Information that was disclosed during term shall remain in effect indefinitely.
[79] 8. Remedies.
[80] a. The Parties acknowledge that the Confidential Information is of a unique and valuable character, and that the unauthorized dissemination of the Confidential Information could cause irreparable harm to the Party and the general public.
[81] b. Therefore, the Parties shall be entitled to injunctive relief preventing the dissemination of any Confidential Information in violation of the terms hereof.
[82] Such injunctive relief shall be in addition to any other remedies available hereunder, whether at law or in equity.
[83] c. The Discloser shall be entitled to recover its costs and fees, including reasonable attorneys' fees, incurred in obtaining any such relief.
[84] The Recipient further acknowledges that the unauthorized disclosure of certain information pertaining to "Critical Assets" or "Critical Infrastructure" may constitute a violation of state and federal law.
[85] 9. Return of JEA Confidential Information.
[86] The Recipient shall immediately return and redeliver to the other all tangible material embodying the JEA Confidential Information provided hereunder and all notes, summaries, memoranda, drawings, manuals, records, excerpts or derivative information deriving there from and all other documents or materials ("Notes") (and all copies of any of the foregoing, including "copies" that have been converted to computerized media in the form of image, data or word processing files either manually or by image capture) based on or including any JEA Confidential Information, in whatever form of storage or retrieval, upon the earlier of -
[87] I. the completion or termination of the dealings between the parties contemplated hereunder; or
[88] II. the termination of this Agreement; or
[89] III. at such time as JEA may so request; provided however that the Recipient may retain such of its documents as is necessary to enable it to comply with its statutory document retention policies.
[90] Alternatively, the Recipient, with the written consent of JEA may (or in the case of Notes, at the Recipient's option) immediately destroy any of the foregoing embodying JEA Confidential Information (or the reasonably non-recoverable data erasure of computerized data) and, upon request, certify in writing such destruction by an authorized officer of the Recipient supervising the destruction).
[91] JEA reserves the right to require evidence supporting such an activity.
[92] 10. Notice of Breach.
[93] The Recipient shall notify the Discloser immediately upon discovery that any Confidential Information has been communicated or distributed to any unauthorized person or entity and will cooperate with efforts by the Discloser to help the Discloser regain possession of Confidential Information and prevent its further unauthorized use.
[94] 11. No Warranty.
[95] The Discloser shall have no liability to the Recipient or the Representatives resulting from any use of the Confidential Information.
[96] The Discloser shall have sole responsibility for providing the Confidential Information necessary for Recipient to perform its obligations under the parties' Agreements.
[97] 12. Miscellaneous.
[98] a. This Agreement:
[99] i. is the complete agreement of the parties concerning the subject matter hereof and supersedes any prior such agreements with respect to further disclosures on such subject matter;
[100] ii. may not be amended or in any manner modified except in writing signed by the parties;
[101] iii. shall be governed and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Florida without regard to its conflict of law provisions; and
[102] iv. shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties and their respective successors, assigns and designees.
[103] b. The Federal and state courts located in Duval County, Florida shall have sole and exclusive jurisdiction over any disputes arising under this Agreement.
[104] If any provision of this Agreement is found to be unenforceable, the remainder shall be enforced as fully as possible and the unenforceable provision shall be deemed modified to the limited extent required to permit its enforcement in a manner most closely representing the intention of the parties as expressed herein.
[105] Any failure by the Discloser to enforce the strict performance of any provision of this Agreement will not constitute a waiver of its right to subsequently enforce such provision or any other provision of this Agreement.
[106] c. Any notices required or permitted to be given hereunder may be delivered by hand, deposited with a nationally recognized overnight carrier, electronic-mail, or mailed by certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, in each case, to the address of the other party first indicated above.
[107] All such notices or communications shall be deemed to have been given and received
[108] (a) in the case of personal delivery or electronic-mail, on the date of such delivery,
[109] (b) in the case of delivery by a nationally recognized overnight carrier, on the third business day following dispatch and
[110] (c) in the case of mailing, on the seventh business day following such mailing.
[111] IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties hereto have executed this Agreement as of the date first above written.

- [P-03] Missing required term. No reverse engineering: The NDA must forbid the counterparty from reverse engineering samples, tooling, prototypes or software that embody our confidential information. Term required/forbidden: The Receiving Party shall not reverse engineer any objects which embody the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
- [P-07] Breaks the rule. Minimum survival period: Confidentiality obligations must survive termination of the NDA for at least 36 months. Term required/forbidden: Confidentiality obligations must survive termination of the NDA for at least 36 months. (segments [75])
- [P-19] Deviates from the rule (bring it back within the rule). Maximum confidentiality term: Confidentiality obligations may not run longer than 120 months unless the General Counsel approves a longer or indefinite term. Term required/forbidden: Confidentiality obligations may not run longer than 120 months unless the General Counsel approves a longer or indefinite term.
- [P-21] Deviates from the rule (bring it back within the rule). Governing law: NDAs must be governed by Ohio or Delaware law unless the General Counsel approves another governing law. Term required/forbidden: NDAs must be governed by Ohio or Delaware law unless the General Counsel approves another governing law. (segments [101])
- [P-29] Missing required term. Employee non-solicitation of colleagues: Employee and contractor-engineer agreements must bind the individual not to solicit our personnel, except where California law governs. Term required/forbidden: The Receiving Party shall not solicit some of the Disclosing Party's representatives.
- [P-30] Missing required term. Trade secret whistleblower immunity notice: Employee agreements governed by US law must include the notice of immunity for confidential disclosure of trade secrets to government officials or an attorney. Term required/forbidden: The agreement includes notice of the immunity for confidential disclosure of trade secrets to government officials or an attorney in reporting a suspected violation of law.
- [CONS-XREF-1004.22] Internal inconsistency. Refers to Section 1004.22, which this NDA does not have. (segments [70])
- [CONS-XREF-119.0713] Internal inconsistency. Refers to Section 119.0713, which this NDA does not have. (segments [18])

DOCUMENT: Code of Business Conduct

# Code of Business Conduct

**Company:** Northwind Cloud, Inc.
**Document owner:** Chief Compliance Officer, reporting to the General Counsel
**Policy number:** CMP-001
**Effective date:** January 20, 2025
**Applies to:** All directors, officers, employees, contractors and interns of Northwind Cloud, Inc. and its subsidiaries

---

## 1. A Message From Our Chief Executive Officer

Northwind earned the trust of its customers one release, one support ticket and one renewal at a time. That trust is the most valuable thing we own, and it can be damaged much faster than it can be built. This Code of Business Conduct (the "Code") describes the standards of honesty, fairness and respect that we expect from each other. It cannot cover every situation. Where it is silent, ask yourself whether you would be comfortable having your decision described in the press, explained to your family and defended to a customer. If you are unsure, ask. Nobody has ever been disciplined at Northwind for asking a question in good faith.

## 2. Purpose and Scope

The Code applies to everyone who works for Northwind Cloud, Inc. ("Northwind") anywhere in the world, to members of the Board of Directors when acting in that role, and to agents and representatives who act on Northwind's behalf. Managers have extra responsibility: they must lead by example, make sure that their teams know the Code and never pressure anyone to break it.

## 3. Definitions

- **Conflict of interest** means a situation in which a personal interest, relationship or outside activity could influence, or appear to influence, a decision made for Northwind.
- **Government official** means anyone who works for or on behalf of a government, a government-owned company, a political party or a public international organization, and includes employees of public universities and public hospitals.
- **Family member** means a spouse or partner, parent, child, sibling, in-law, grandparent, grandchild and anyone who shares your household.
- **Ethics hotline** means the independent, third-party reporting service available around the clock by phone and web.
- **Compliance Office** means the Chief Compliance Officer and the team who administer the Code.

## 4. Our Core Principles

1. **We obey the law.** We comply with the laws and regulations of every place where we operate.
2. **We deal honestly.** We do not lie, mislead, cheat or steal, and we keep our promises.
3. **We treat people with respect.** We value diversity, and we do not tolerate harassment, discrimination or retaliation.
4. **We put customers first.** We build products that serve customers well and we are straightforward about their strengths and limits.
5. **We protect what we are trusted with.** We guard company assets and the property of others.
6. **We speak up.** We raise concerns early and support others who do.

## 5. Respect in the Workplace

### 5.1 Equal opportunity

Northwind provides equal employment opportunity to all workers and applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by law. Decisions about hiring, pay, promotion, discipline and termination are made on merit.

### 5.2 Harassment

Harassment, whether sexual, racial or of any other kind, is prohibited in the office, at company events, online and in any setting connected to work. Harassment includes unwelcome comments, jokes, images, messages, touching, exclusion and threats. Workers who experience or witness it should report it to their manager, Human Resources or the ethics hotline.

### 5.3 Accommodation

Northwind will make reasonable accommodations for disability, pregnancy and religious practice unless doing so would cause undue hardship. Workers who need an accommodation should contact Human Resources.

### 5.4 Health and safety

Northwind provides a safe workplace. Workers must follow safety rules, report hazards and injuries immediately, and never work under the influence of alcohol or illegal drugs. Violence or threats of violence are not tolerated, and weapons are not allowed on company premises.

## 6. Conflicts of Interest

### 6.1 General rule

Workers must avoid situations where their personal interests conflict, or appear to conflict, with their duties to Northwind. When a conflict cannot be avoided, it must be disclosed to the manager and the Compliance Office as soon as it arises.

### 6.2 Common conflicts

Examples requiring disclosure and approval include:

- a financial interest of more than one percent in a company that is a competitor, customer or vendor of Northwind;
- hiring, supervising or influencing the pay of a family member;
- accepting a position as a director, adviser or employee of another company, particularly a competitor or vendor;
- using Northwind's time, equipment or information for outside business activities;
- directing company business to a firm in which you or a family member has an interest; and
- taking for yourself an opportunity that you learn about through your work for Northwind.

### 6.3 Review

The Compliance Office reviews each disclosure and decides whether to approve it, require changes or prohibit it. Decisions are recorded, and approvals are reviewed annually. Conflicts involving officers or directors are decided by the Audit Committee.

## 7. Gifts, Meals and Entertainment

Workers may give or receive gifts, meals and entertainment only if they are modest, infrequent, legal, openly given, consistent with accepted business custom and not intended to influence a business decision. A single gift with a value over $100, or any gift from a firm that is taking part in a tender, must be disclosed to the Compliance Office. Cash and cash equivalents are never allowed. Gifts to government officials are subject to special rules and require the General Counsel's approval in advance.

## 8. Anti-Corruption and Anti-Bribery

Northwind prohibits bribery in any form. Workers must not offer, promise, give, request or accept anything of value to improperly influence a decision or to obtain an advantage, whether the recipient is a public official or a private person. The U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, the U.K. Bribery Act and similar laws apply to Northwind everywhere in the world. Workers must not make facilitation payments, and must be careful when engaging resellers, consultants and other intermediaries, who must be vetted by the Compliance Office before they work for Northwind. Political contributions and charitable donations in Northwind's name require the Chief Executive Officer's and General Counsel's approval.

## 9. Fair Competition

Northwind competes vigorously and fairly. Workers must not agree with competitors on prices, discounts, bids, customers, territories or output, and must not exchange competitively sensitive information with competitors, including at trade associations and conferences. Workers must not make false or misleading statements about competitors' products, and may gather competitive intelligence only from public sources or ethically obtained information. Questions about pricing practices, bundling, exclusivity or dealings with resellers should go to the Legal Department before action is taken.

## 10. Sales Practices and Accuracy With Customers

Salespeople must describe the platform accurately and avoid promising features, dates or service levels that are not approved. Order forms must be complete and accurate, and nothing may be promised through informal assurances. Revenue must be recorded only when it has been earned under the company's accounting policies. Workers must never alter dates, backdate documents or shift revenue to meet a target.

## 11. Accurate Books and Records

Northwind's books, records and financial statements must be complete, accurate and timely. Workers must never falsify documents, create off-the-books accounts, misclassify expenses or conceal transactions. Anyone who becomes aware of any questionable accounting or auditing matter should report it to the Chief Financial Officer, the Compliance Office or the ethics hotline. Reports about accounting matters go directly to the Audit Committee. Workers must cooperate with auditors and must never mislead or pressure them.

## 12. Insider Trading

Workers who learn material non-public information about Northwind or other companies, such as unreleased financial results, pending acquisitions, major customer wins or losses or security incidents, must not buy or sell securities on the basis of it, and must not pass it on to others. Directors, officers and designated employees may trade in Northwind securities only during open trading windows and with pre-clearance from the General Counsel.

## 13. Protecting Company Assets

Workers must use company assets, including funds, equipment, software and the Northwind name, only for legitimate business purposes. Theft, carelessness and waste have a direct impact on the company's profitability. Details of acceptable system use appear in the Information Security Acceptable Use Policy.

## 14. International Business

Northwind complies with export controls, economic sanctions and customs laws. Workers must not engage with parties on the U.S. sanctions lists, and must check with the Compliance Office before dealing with a country or entity that is subject to restriction. Northwind does not take part in boycotts that violate U.S. law. Workers who work with colleagues or customers in other countries should respect local laws and customs, and apply the higher of local law and this Code where they differ.

## 15. Working With Governments

Dealings with government customers and public bodies are subject to special rules on procurement, gifts, lobbying and conflicts. Workers who work on government business must follow the Public Sector Handbook. Any inquiry from a regulator, law enforcement agency or investigator should be sent to the Legal Department immediately.

## 16. Communications and Social Media

Only designated spokespersons may speak for Northwind to the media, analysts and investors. Workers who receive an inquiry should refer it to Communications. Workers may use social media in their personal lives but must be clear that they speak for themselves, must not disclose non-public information about Northwind, and must not harass others.

## 17. Raising Concerns and Non-Retaliation

### 17.1 How to raise a concern

Workers who believe the Code, a law or a company policy has been or may be violated should speak to their manager, Human Resources, the Compliance Office, the Legal Department or the ethics hotline. Reports may be made anonymously where the law allows.

### 17.2 Investigations

The Compliance Office reviews each report promptly and decides who should investigate. Investigations are fair, thorough and as discreet as possible. Workers must cooperate and tell the truth. They must not interfere with an investigation or discuss it with others except as directed.

### 17.3 Non-retaliation

Northwind forbids retaliation against anyone who reports a concern in good faith or takes part in an investigation. Retaliation is itself a violation of the Code and will lead to discipline.

## 18. Accountability and Discipline

Violating the Code or the law can lead to discipline, up to and including termination, and may lead to civil or criminal penalties. Managers who direct or approve violations, or who fail to act when they know of them, are also accountable. Disciplinary decisions are made consistently by Human Resources with the Compliance Office. Waivers of the Code for directors and executive officers may be granted only by the Board and will be disclosed as required by law.

## 19. Training and Annual Certification

All workers complete Code training on joining and every year, and certify that they have read and understood the Code and have disclosed any actual or potential conflicts. Managers also complete training on handling reports and avoiding retaliation. Completion rates are reported to the Audit Committee.

## Appendix A. Questions to Ask Before You Act

1. Is it legal?
2. Is it consistent with the Code and Northwind's policies?
3. Does it treat customers, colleagues, partners and the company fairly?
4. Would I be comfortable if it were reported in the news?
5. Would I be comfortable explaining it to my manager and the Compliance Office?
6. Is there any chance that it benefits me personally at the expense of Northwind?
7. If I am unsure, have I asked someone who can help?

## Appendix B. Examples of Situations to Raise

**A vendor offers season tickets to a major league baseball team.** Politely decline or consult the Compliance Office. Season tickets are not modest or infrequent, and the vendor may have a bid before Northwind.

**A manager asks a team member to record a sale in the quarter even though the customer has not yet signed.** This is improper revenue recognition. Report it to the Chief Financial Officer or the ethics hotline.

**A colleague's spouse owns a company that bids for a Northwind purchase.** The colleague must disclose the relationship and must not take part in the decision.

**A friend at a competitor asks about next quarter's pricing.** Do not discuss it. Competitively sensitive information must not be exchanged with competitors.

**A teammate frequently makes jokes about a coworker's accent.** This may be harassment. Report it to Human Resources or the ethics hotline, or speak to the manager.

**A customer's procurement officer hints that a gift would help the renewal go smoothly.** Decline and report it to the Compliance Office at once.

## Appendix C. Ethics Hotline Operating Procedures

The ethics hotline is operated by an independent provider and is available in more than twenty languages, around the clock. Callers may remain anonymous. The provider gives each reporter an access code, so that they can follow up and answer questions without revealing their identity. Reports are sent to the Chief Compliance Officer, or, for matters concerning the Compliance Office, the Chair of the Audit Committee. The Compliance Office acknowledges reports within two business days, opens a case, assigns an investigator and gives the reporter progress updates where possible. The Compliance Office reports statistics to the Audit Committee every quarter, including the number and type of reports, time to close, substantiation rates and outcomes.

## Appendix D. Investigation Principles

Investigations follow principles of fairness and proportionality. Investigators remain impartial and declare any conflicts. They gather facts from documents and interviews, give the subject an opportunity to respond, and document their findings. Where appropriate, they recommend remedial steps, such as training, process changes, discipline or reports to authorities. Human Resources is consulted before discipline. Records of investigations are kept by the Compliance Office for seven years and are available to the Audit Committee.

## Appendix E. Community Involvement

Northwind encourages workers to take part in their communities. The company offers each worker two paid days a year to volunteer with a charity of their choice and matches donations up to $1,000 per worker per year to registered nonprofit organizations. Workers must make clear that they speak for themselves when taking part in community or political activity, and must not use company time or resources for political campaigns.

## 20. Revision History

| Version | Date | Author | Summary of change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | June 1, 2018 | Compliance Office | Initial issue |
| 2.0 | September 8, 2021 | Compliance Office | Added insider trading and sales practices |
| 2.3 | February 14, 2023 | Compliance Office | Revised gifts thresholds; added international business |
| 3.0 | January 20, 2025 | Compliance Office | Rewritten in plain language; added communications section |

DOCUMENT: Confidentiality and NDA Standard

# Confidentiality and NDA Standard

**Company:** Northwind Cloud, Inc.
**Document owner:** Office of the General Counsel
**Policy number:** LEG-004
**Effective date:** March 1, 2025
**Applies to:** All employees, contractors and officers of Northwind Cloud, Inc. and its subsidiaries

---

## 1. Purpose

Northwind Cloud, Inc. ("Northwind", "we", "us") builds and operates a multi-tenant software-as-a-service platform for enterprise customers in North America and Europe. Our customers, vendors and partners trust us with source code, product roadmaps, pricing, security architecture, customer lists and, very often, personal data about their own employees and clients. Our own competitive position depends on the same kind of information flowing in the other direction.

This Standard sets out how Northwind classifies and protects confidential information, who is allowed to see it, and the minimum protections the Legal Department expects to find in the written agreements that govern our exchange of such information with outside parties. It is intended to give business teams a single, practical reference so that they can move quickly on commercial opportunities without exposing the company to avoidable risk.

## 2. Scope and Definitions

### 2.1 Scope

This Standard applies to every Northwind worker and to all information that Northwind creates, receives or holds, in any form: electronic files, source repositories, tickets, chat messages, slide decks, whiteboards, printed pages and spoken remarks. It applies in every office, in remote work locations and on any device used for company business.

### 2.2 Definitions

- **Confidential Information** means non-public information that Northwind or a third party has entrusted to Northwind and that a reasonable person would understand to be sensitive. It includes information that is not labelled.
- **Counterparty** means a customer, vendor, partner, prospective employee or other outside person or company with which Northwind exchanges Confidential Information.
- **Disclosing party** and **receiving party** mean, in any given exchange, the party that shares information and the party that receives it. In a two-way exchange each party is both.
- **Information Owner** means the Northwind executive accountable for a body of information, for example the Chief Technology Officer for source code or the Chief Financial Officer for unreleased financial results.
- **Deal Owner** means the Northwind employee sponsoring a commercial relationship with a Counterparty.
- **Legal Reviewer** means an attorney, paralegal or contract specialist in the Legal Department who has been assigned to a request.

## 3. Classification of Information

### 3.1 Classification levels

Northwind uses four levels. Each level has handling rules that apply regardless of the medium in which the information is held.

| Level | Description | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Public | Approved for release to anyone | Marketing pages, published documentation, press releases |
| Internal | Meant for workers only; low harm if exposed | Org charts, internal wiki pages, meeting notes |
| Confidential | Harm to Northwind or a Counterparty if exposed | Customer lists, pricing models, unreleased roadmaps, contract drafts |
| Restricted | Severe harm if exposed; need-to-know only | Source code for core services, encryption keys, security assessments, unreleased financial results, personal data in bulk |

### 3.2 Who classifies

The Information Owner sets the classification of the information in their charge. A worker who creates a document and is unsure of its level should treat it as Confidential until the Information Owner or the Security team says otherwise. Information received from a Counterparty takes the level that the Counterparty's own labelling or the nature of the information suggests, and never a level below Confidential.

### 3.3 Reclassification

Information may be reclassified downward only by the Information Owner, and only after consulting the Security team. A record of the decision must be kept in the document management system. Information may be reclassified upward by any manager who believes the existing level is too low.

## 4. Protections We Expect in Counterparty Agreements

This Part describes what the Legal Department looks for when Northwind signs, or asks a Counterparty to sign, a written agreement for the exchange of Confidential Information. The Legal Department publishes the model language separately in the clause library; this Standard states the principle behind each protection. A Deal Owner may not agree to depart from these protections without the approvals described in Part 7.

### 4.1 Purpose of use

Every agreement we sign or propose must limit the receiving party's use of our information to the purposes the agreement itself states, and no other purpose. The stated purpose should be specific enough that a reader outside the deal team can tell whether a proposed use falls inside it, for example "evaluating a potential subscription to the Northwind platform" rather than "business purposes".

### 4.2 Spoken disclosures

Information that we share in meetings, calls or demonstrations must be covered even though it is spoken and never written down. Product engineers regularly give architecture walkthroughs and security briefings that are never followed by a written summary, and an agreement that protects only documents would leave those conversations exposed.

### 4.3 Duties that continue

The agreement must make clear that the duties of confidence continue to bind the parties after the agreement has ended or expired. How long those duties continue is addressed in Part 6 and in the Records Retention and Disposal Policy, which sets the outer limit on how long Northwind can administer them.

### 4.4 Legal compulsion

If the other side is compelled by law, regulation or a court or agency process to disclose our information, it must tell us before it does so. Prompt notice gives us the chance to seek a protective order or to narrow the request. When Northwind is itself the subject of a subpoena or a government request, the General Counsel decides how to respond and no worker may reply directly.

### 4.5 No grant of rights

No clause may be read as handing the other side a licence, ownership interest or any other right in the information we disclose. Where a commercial relationship does involve a licence, that licence belongs in a separate, signed commercial agreement. The Intellectual Property Policy explains how Northwind treats ownership of information more generally.

### 4.6 Protections for information received

When Northwind receives Counterparty information, workers must follow the handling rules in Part 8 of this Standard, store the information only in approved systems, and record the receipt in the deal file.

## 5. Customer and Partner Relationships

### 5.1 Breadth of the definition

In agreements with customers and partners, the definition of protected information must reach business, financial and commercial information and may not be confined to technical material alone. Our enterprise customers routinely share procurement plans, user volumes and budget constraints with our sales engineers, and our partners share go-to-market plans that have no technical content at all.

### 5.2 Hiring and approaching people

An agreement with a customer must not bar either side from approaching or hiring the other side's people. Our customers include some of the largest employers in the sectors we serve, and a clause of this kind could limit our own recruiting in ways that the business has never approved. Restrictions of this kind in partner relationships are handled under the Contract Approval Matrix.

### 5.3 The relationship itself

The other side must agree not to reveal that the parties have negotiated or entered into the agreement. Several of our customers are named reference accounts only after their own communications teams have cleared a case study, and an early leak of a pending deal can affect both sides' negotiations with others.

### 5.4 Remembered information

We never accept a clause that lets the other side keep using whatever it happens to remember from our information, often called a residuals clause. Our engineers and product managers talk to Counterparty staff at length, and such a clause would permit the other side's staff to carry away and reuse what they learned.

## 6. Duration of Protection

### 6.1 Minimum period

The duty of confidence must run for at least 24 months. Any shorter period needs written approval from the Deputy General Counsel before the agreement is signed. When personal data is involved, the longer minimum in the Data Protection and Privacy Policy applies instead.

### 6.2 Maximum period

The duty of confidence may not be stated to run for more than 60 months. Open-ended obligations are difficult to administer, cannot be monitored by the business, and conflict with the records schedule.

### 6.3 Surviving obligations

Obligations that survive the end of the agreement must survive for at least 24 months. The upper limit on how long such obligations may be stated to survive is set in the Records Retention and Disposal Policy.

## 7. Exceptions and Approvals

A request to depart from any protection in Parts 4 through 6 is made through the Legal Intake portal. The Legal Reviewer will record the proposed departure, the business reason and the compensating controls offered. Approvals are given by the persons named in the relevant section, or, where none is named, by the General Counsel. Approval is granted in writing, applies to one agreement only, and does not create a precedent for later requests. The Legal Department keeps a register of approvals for audit purposes.

## 8. Handling Rules for Confidential and Restricted Information

### 8.1 Storage

Confidential and Restricted information must be stored only in systems approved by the Security team: the company document management system, the engineering source-control platform and the corporate cloud storage tenant. Personal cloud accounts, personal email and unapproved messaging tools must not be used.

### 8.2 Sharing inside Northwind

Access to Restricted information is granted by the Information Owner on a need-to-know basis and reviewed every quarter. Access to Confidential information may be granted by a department head. Access is removed on the day a worker changes roles or leaves the company.

### 8.3 Sharing outside Northwind

Before Confidential or Restricted information is sent to anyone outside Northwind, the sender must confirm that a signed agreement is in place with the recipient, using the Legal Intake portal's lookup tool. Information may be transmitted only by approved secure channels. Restricted information must additionally be encrypted in transit and at rest.

### 8.4 Printing and physical media

Restricted information must not be printed except with the Information Owner's approval. Printed Confidential information must be collected from the printer promptly, kept in a locked drawer when unattended and destroyed in a cross-cut shredder or a locked shred bin. Removable media may be used only with encryption and must be registered with IT.

### 8.5 Meetings and public places

Workers must not discuss Confidential or Restricted matters in elevators, restaurants, airports, co-working lounges or other public places where they might be overheard. Video calls involving Restricted information must use a private room or headphones. Workers must not leave screens unlocked.

### 8.6 Visitors

Visitors to Northwind offices must sign in at reception, wear a visitor badge and be escorted at all times. Whiteboards in meeting rooms must be erased after use, and meeting rooms must be checked for left-behind documents.

## 9. Roles and Responsibilities

- **General Counsel** owns this Standard, approves exceptions where no other approver is named and reports to the Audit Committee annually on compliance.
- **Deputy General Counsel** supervises the Legal Intake process and approves the departures assigned to that office.
- **Information Owners** classify information, grant access and review access lists every quarter.
- **Deal Owners** identify at the outset of a relationship what information will be exchanged, request a Legal Reviewer through the Legal Intake portal and keep the deal file complete.
- **Legal Reviewers** review requests, apply this Standard and record exceptions in the register.
- **The Security team** maintains approved systems, investigates suspected exposure and advises on classification.
- **Managers** make sure their teams complete training and follow this Standard.
- **All workers** protect the information entrusted to them and report suspected exposure immediately.

## 10. Training and Awareness

All new workers complete confidentiality training within their first two weeks and annually after that. Engineers with access to Restricted source code complete an additional module on secure handling. The Legal Department runs quarterly lunch-and-learn sessions for sales and customer success teams, focused on the questions most often raised in the Legal Intake portal. Completion is tracked by Human Resources and reported to department heads each quarter.

## 11. Reporting a Suspected Exposure

A worker who suspects that Confidential or Restricted information has been lost, misdirected or accessed without authority must report it at once to the Security team through the incident hotline or the security mailbox. The report should say what information was involved, who might have seen it, when it happened and whether any Counterparty is affected. The Security team opens an incident and the General Counsel decides whether a Counterparty or regulator must be notified. No worker may contact a Counterparty about a suspected exposure without the General Counsel's approval. Reports made in good faith are never grounds for discipline.

## 12. Monitoring and Audit

The Security team monitors access to Restricted repositories and reviews unusual download or sharing activity. Internal Audit samples signed counterparty agreements each year and reports the results to the General Counsel and the Audit Committee. The sample covers whether the Legal Intake portal was used, whether approvals were recorded and whether the deal file is complete. Findings are tracked until closed.

## 13. Enforcement

A breach of this Standard may lead to disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment or contract, and, where the law allows, civil or criminal referral. Managers who knowingly allow a breach, or who retaliate against a worker for reporting one, are also subject to discipline. The General Counsel may suspend a worker's access to Confidential and Restricted information while an investigation is under way.

## 14. Relationship to Other Policies

This Standard should be read with the Vendor and Third-Party Risk Policy, the Data Protection and Privacy Policy, the Contract Approval Matrix, the Intellectual Property Policy, the Records Retention and Disposal Policy and the Information Security Acceptable Use Policy. If this Standard conflicts with a more specific policy on the same subject, the more specific policy controls, unless the General Counsel decides otherwise in writing.

## Appendix A. Frequently Asked Questions

**Who decides what classification a customer's data takes?** The Information Owner for the relevant system decides, in consultation with the Security team. Customer content hosted in the platform is always treated as Restricted, because Northwind cannot know what each customer has stored.

**May I take a Confidential document home?** Only on a company-managed device and only if you need to work on it outside the office. Do not print it at home, and do not leave it open where family members or visitors can see the screen.

**May I forward a Confidential email to my personal account so that I can read it on my phone?** No. Install the approved mobile application and read it there. Forwarding company mail to personal accounts is prohibited by the Information Security Acceptable Use Policy.

**What do I do if I receive something that was clearly not meant for me?** Stop reading, do not forward it, tell the sender and the Security team, and delete it once they confirm. If the material appears to belong to another company, tell the Legal Department as well.

**Can I mention a customer's name in a conference talk?** Only if the customer has approved the use in writing through Marketing. Customer names, logos and metrics are Confidential until they are approved for reference use.

**How long should I keep my own notes?** Notes of meetings that evidence a decision or commitment should be saved to the deal file. Personal scratch notes should be destroyed when they are no longer useful, in line with the Records Retention and Disposal Policy.

## Appendix B. Examples of Classification

| Item | Level | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Public product documentation | Public | Published on the website |
| Quarterly all-hands slides without financials | Internal | Of interest to staff only |
| A customer's usage report | Confidential | Contains the customer's business metrics |
| Production database snapshot | Restricted | Contains personal data in bulk |
| Unreleased pricing proposal | Confidential | Harm if competitors see it |
| Signing keys for software releases | Restricted | Compromise would affect every customer |
| Board materials before release | Restricted | Material non-public information |
| Interview notes about a job candidate | Confidential | Personal and sensitive |
| Penetration test report | Restricted | Details unpatched weaknesses |
| Sales call recording | Confidential | May contain customer business plans and personal data |

## Appendix C. Responsibilities Checklist for Deal Owners

Before sharing information with a Counterparty, the Deal Owner should be able to answer yes to each of the following.

1. Is the information at the lowest level of detail needed for the purpose?
2. Has the Information Owner agreed that it can be shared?
3. Has a Legal Reviewer been assigned, and is the signed paperwork on file?
4. Will the information be sent through an approved channel?
5. Is the list of Counterparty recipients known and recorded in the deal file?
6. Is a date set for review of what has been shared and for what must be returned or removed?
7. Does the deal file record the Northwind people who have been told about the exchange?

## Appendix D. Quarterly Access Review Procedure

Each quarter the Security team sends every Information Owner a list of the people who hold access to their Restricted information. The owner confirms, removes or queries each entry within ten business days. Entries not confirmed in time are removed automatically. The Security team keeps the results for three years and sends a summary to the General Counsel. Owners should look especially for people who have changed teams, contractors whose engagements have ended and accounts that have not been used in ninety days.

## 15. Review and Revision History

The General Counsel reviews this Standard at least once a year, and sooner if the law, the business or an incident calls for it.

| Version | Date | Author | Summary of change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | March 4, 2021 | Office of the General Counsel | Initial issue |
| 1.1 | June 15, 2022 | Office of the General Counsel | Added classification table; clarified Deal Owner duties |
| 2.0 | February 6, 2024 | Office of the General Counsel | Restructured Parts 4 through 6; added Legal Intake portal |
| 2.1 | March 1, 2025 | Office of the General Counsel | Updated handling rules for remote work; aligned with records schedule |

# Data Protection and Privacy Policy

**Company:** Northwind Cloud, Inc.
**Document owner:** Privacy Office, reporting to the General Counsel
**Policy number:** PRV-002
**Effective date:** April 1, 2025
**Applies to:** All Northwind workers, and all systems and vendors that process personal data for Northwind

---

## 1. Purpose and Scope

Northwind Cloud, Inc. ("Northwind") processes personal data in two capacities. As a **processor** (service provider), it hosts and handles personal data that enterprise customers place in the Northwind platform: their employees' names and business contact details, their end customers' account records, usage logs, support transcripts and in some cases payroll or benefits data. As a **controller** (business), it handles the personal data of its own workers, job applicants, website visitors, prospects and the employees of its customers and vendors.

This Policy sets out the principles Northwind follows to protect personal data, the duties of the people who handle it, and the specific controls that apply to common situations, including exchanges of personal data with customers, vendors and partners and transfers outside the United States. It supports compliance with the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act (CCPA/CPRA), the Virginia, Colorado and Connecticut privacy statutes, the New York SHIELD Act, the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and UK GDPR, and Northwind's contractual commitments to customers.

## 2. Definitions

- **Personal data** means any information relating to an identified or identifiable individual, including names, email addresses, IP addresses, device identifiers, account numbers, location data, employment records and any inference drawn from such data.
- **Sensitive personal data** means personal data revealing government identifiers, financial account credentials, precise geolocation, health information, racial or ethnic origin, religious belief, union membership, biometric identifiers, or the personal data of a child.
- **Processing** means any operation performed on personal data, including collection, storage, use, disclosure, transfer and deletion.
- **Controller / business** and **processor / service provider** have the meanings given in the applicable law.
- **Data subject** means the individual to whom personal data relates.
- **Privacy Office** means the Chief Privacy Officer and the team of privacy counsel and analysts reporting to the General Counsel.
- **Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA)** means a structured assessment of the privacy risk of a proposed processing activity.
- **Restricted transfer** means a transfer of personal data from the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom or Switzerland to a country that has not been found to provide adequate protection.

## 3. Exchanging Personal Data With Outside Parties

### 3.1 Protection that does not depend on labels

Where personal data will be exchanged, protection may not depend on the disclosing party marking or labelling the information as confidential. Personal data arrives in Northwind in bulk, in support tickets, logs, screenshots and spreadsheets, and nobody can reasonably be expected to label every record. The obligation to protect personal data attaches to the nature of the data, not to the presence of a stamp.

### 3.2 Minimization before sharing

Before sending personal data to a customer, vendor or partner, the sender must ask whether the purpose can be met with less. Where it can, the sender must remove, mask, pseudonymize or aggregate the data first. Direct identifiers must not be sent when a stable internal identifier would do.

### 3.3 Approved channels

Personal data may be exchanged only through channels approved by the Security team: the customer portal, the managed secure file transfer service, the encrypted email gateway, and APIs authenticated with credentials issued through the secrets manager. Personal data must never be sent through consumer messaging apps, personal email or unmanaged file-sharing tools.

### 3.4 Records of disclosures

Each time Northwind discloses personal data to a third party outside a standard integration, the sender records in the privacy register the date, the recipient, the categories of data, the purpose and the legal basis. The register is reviewed by the Privacy Office each quarter.

## 4. International Transfers

### 4.1 Cross-border transfer mechanism

When personal data is transferred to or from a counterparty outside the United States, the agreement must incorporate the EU Standard Contractual Clauses or an equivalent transfer mechanism approved by the Privacy Office. The Privacy Office maintains the approved mechanisms, which at present are the Standard Contractual Clauses (controller-to-processor and processor-to-processor modules), the UK International Data Transfer Addendum and the Swiss addendum, together with certification under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework where the recipient holds one.

### 4.2 Transfer impact assessments

For each restricted transfer the Privacy Office completes a transfer impact assessment that considers the laws of the destination country, the access powers of its public authorities, the supplementary measures proposed and the sensitivity of the data. The assessment is refreshed annually and whenever the destination country's laws change materially.

### 4.3 Data localization commitments

Northwind offers EU customers hosting in the Frankfurt and Dublin regions. Engineers and support staff must not move customer personal data out of the region selected by the customer, except as the customer instructs or as needed to resolve a support case under the controls in the support runbook.

## 5. Duration of Protection

### 5.1 Longer protection for personal data

When personal data is involved, the duty of confidence must last at least 36 months. The longer period reflects the time over which a leak of personal data can be used for fraud, identity theft or targeted phishing. The general minimum and maximum periods that apply to all other exchanges are in the Confidentiality and NDA Standard.

## 6. Principles of Processing

Northwind follows these principles in every processing activity.

1. **Lawfulness, fairness and transparency.** Every processing activity has a documented legal basis, and individuals are told in clear language what is done with their data.
2. **Purpose limitation.** Personal data is collected for specified purposes and is not used in ways incompatible with them.
3. **Data minimization.** Only the data needed for the purpose is collected and retained.
4. **Accuracy.** Reasonable steps are taken to keep data accurate and up to date.
5. **Storage limitation.** Personal data is kept no longer than necessary, as set in the Records Retention and Disposal Policy.
6. **Integrity and confidentiality.** Appropriate technical and organizational measures protect the data.
7. **Accountability.** Northwind can demonstrate compliance through records, assessments and audits.

## 7. Roles and Responsibilities

- **Chief Privacy Officer (CPO)** owns this Policy, advises the business, chairs the Privacy Council and reports to the Audit Committee quarterly.
- **Privacy Office** maintains the register of processing activities, runs DPIAs and transfer assessments, handles data subject requests and regulator inquiries, and reviews vendor and customer terms involving personal data.
- **Chief Information Security Officer** is responsible for technical and organizational security measures and for breach detection.
- **Product and Engineering leaders** build privacy into design (privacy by design and by default) and ensure data flows are documented.
- **Data Owners** are accountable for each dataset, including its purpose, legal basis, retention and access.
- **All workers** complete privacy training, handle personal data only as needed for their roles and report suspected incidents immediately.

## 8. Data Subject Rights

Individuals may have the right to access, correct, delete, port or restrict the use of their personal data, to opt out of sale, sharing or targeted advertising, and to object to certain processing. The Privacy Office operates a request portal and a toll-free number. Requests are verified, logged and answered within the statutory period, generally 45 days under U.S. state laws and one month under GDPR. Where Northwind acts as a processor, it forwards the request to the customer within five business days and assists the customer in responding, as the data processing addendum provides. Workers who receive a request by any channel must forward it to the Privacy Office the same day and must not respond themselves.

## 9. Privacy by Design and DPIAs

A DPIA is required before launching a new product feature, vendor or data use that involves sensitive personal data, large-scale profiling, systematic monitoring, automated decision-making that significantly affects individuals, or new use of existing data for an incompatible purpose. The product manager prepares the DPIA with the Privacy Office, which documents risks, mitigations and residual risk. High residual risks are escalated to the Privacy Council and may be accepted only by the Chief Privacy Officer.

## 10. Security of Personal Data

Personal data must be protected by controls proportionate to its sensitivity. At a minimum:

- sensitive personal data and data at rest in production are encrypted using current standards, with keys held in the managed key service;
- access is role-based, reviewed quarterly and logged;
- production personal data is not copied into development or test environments, except in masked form;
- logs and backups containing personal data are subject to the same retention limits as primary stores; and
- engineers handling personal data in support cases use the break-glass procedure, which requires a ticket reference and generates an access record.

## 11. Personal Data Breaches

A worker who suspects a personal data breach must report it to the Security team immediately. The Security team and the Privacy Office decide within 24 hours whether a breach has occurred and assess its scope. Where a breach affects customer personal data, Northwind notifies the affected customers without undue delay and in any event within 48 hours of confirming it, so that they can meet their own legal duties. Where Northwind is the controller, the General Counsel decides whether notice to regulators and individuals is required under state law, the GDPR (72 hours) or other applicable rules. All breaches, whether or not notified, are recorded in the incident register with the facts, effects and remedial action.

## 12. Vendors and Sub-processors

Vendors that process personal data for Northwind must pass the security and privacy review described in the Vendor and Third-Party Risk Policy, sign a data processing addendum reflecting this Policy, flow the same obligations down to their own sub-processors and support Northwind in meeting data subject requests and breach duties. The Privacy Office maintains the public list of Northwind's sub-processors and gives customers advance notice of changes.

## 13. Marketing and Communications

Marketing campaigns must respect opt-out and consent records. Cookies and similar technologies on Northwind's websites are managed through a consent banner that applies the visitor's regional setting. Email lists are not purchased or rented. Customer testimonials and logos are used only with written permission from the customer's authorized representative.

## 14. Employee and Applicant Data

Human Resources handles employee and applicant data under the Employee Privacy Notice. Access is limited to HR, the employee's management chain and, where necessary, Legal and Finance. Background checks are performed only where permitted by law, with consent where required. Monitoring of work systems is carried out under the Information Security Acceptable Use Policy and is limited to what is necessary for security and compliance.

## 15. Training and Awareness

All workers complete privacy training on joining and annually. Engineers, support staff and sales teams complete role-specific modules. The Privacy Office publishes quarterly bulletins and holds office hours every week.

## 16. Audit and Enforcement

The Privacy Office tests compliance through quarterly control reviews, and Internal Audit examines the program each year. Violations may result in disciplinary action up to termination, and in some cases civil or criminal penalties for the individuals involved. Workers who report concerns in good faith are protected from retaliation.

## Appendix A. Categories of Personal Data Northwind Handles

| Category | Examples | Typical source | Typical purpose | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Customer user data | Names, work emails, job titles, login history | Customer administrators | Provide the service | Medium |
| End-customer records | Account numbers, transaction history, addresses | Customer uploads | Provide the service | High |
| Support data | Tickets, screenshots, call recordings | Customer users | Resolve cases | Medium to high |
| Usage telemetry | Device identifiers, IP addresses, feature use | Platform | Operate and improve the service | Low to medium |
| Prospect data | Business contact details, event attendance | Marketing | Sales outreach | Low |
| Worker data | Payroll, benefits, performance reviews, identifiers | Workers | Employment administration | High |
| Applicant data | Resumes, interview notes, references | Candidates | Recruiting | Medium |
| Vendor contact data | Names and business emails of vendor staff | Vendors | Manage relationships | Low |

## Appendix B. Lawful Bases Under GDPR

Where GDPR applies, each processing activity relies on one of the following bases, which the Privacy Office records in the register of processing activities: performance of a contract with the individual; compliance with a legal obligation; the legitimate interests of Northwind or a third party, after a balancing test; consent that is freely given, specific, informed and withdrawable; protection of vital interests; or the performance of a task in the public interest. Northwind relies on consent for non-essential cookies and certain marketing, and on legitimate interests for security monitoring, service improvement and fraud prevention. For processing carried out as a processor, the customer determines the basis.

## Appendix C. Data Subject Request Handling Steps

1. **Receive.** The request arrives through the portal, email, phone or any worker. Workers forward requests to the Privacy Office the same day.
2. **Verify.** The Privacy Office confirms the requester's identity using information already held, without collecting more sensitive data than necessary.
3. **Classify.** The request is classified as access, deletion, correction, portability, opt-out or objection. Requests relating to customer content are redirected to the customer, with the requester informed.
4. **Search.** The Privacy Office asks system owners to search their systems, using the data map.
5. **Assess.** Legal reviews any exemptions, for example data needed to defend legal claims or comply with the records schedule.
6. **Respond.** The response is sent in the statutory period, with an explanation of any refusal and of the right to appeal.
7. **Record.** The request, decision and evidence are logged and retained for three years.

## Appendix D. Privacy Metrics

The Privacy Office reports each quarter on: the number of data subject requests received and the median time to complete them; DPIAs completed and open; sub-processors added and removed; privacy incidents by severity; training completion; and the number of vendors with a current data processing addendum. The Audit Committee reviews the report and may ask for deeper analysis of any area.

## Appendix E. Children's Data

Northwind's services are intended for business users and are not directed at children under 16. Workers must not knowingly collect personal data from children. If a worker learns that a child's data has been collected, they must tell the Privacy Office, which will arrange deletion unless the law requires otherwise. Customers who use the platform to process children's data, such as schools, are responsible for obtaining any necessary parental permissions and are reminded of this in the data processing addendum.

## 17. Revision History

| Version | Date | Author | Summary of change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | August 12, 2019 | Privacy Office | Initial issue following CCPA readiness project |
| 1.3 | January 5, 2021 | Privacy Office | Added international transfer section after Schrems II |
| 2.0 | December 9, 2022 | Privacy Office | Updated for CPRA, Virginia and Colorado laws |
| 2.2 | April 1, 2025 | Privacy Office | Added Data Privacy Framework certification; aligned with records schedule |
